segments.text: Let me show you something. This is a live engine. Every point is a word it knows, and every line is a relationship it worked out for itself. Nobody drew this.
Here's Neuron. I'll ask it to define a word it has never been given.
Watch the stage. It goes and reads, finds the word's relationships, and works them into the graph, along with everything it met on the way.
That one line set off a whole tree of runs underneath it. Every run leaves a receipt, so let's open this one and play it back.
This is the path it took through the graph, hop by hop. Not a summary of it. The actual path.
Now I'll ask the same thing again. Nothing runs. It already knows. Learning happens once. Recall is instant.

And this is Cortex. Same engine, different job. I tell it about a project in plain lines: what it is, where the checkpoints are, how things stand. Each line lands with its own time, so the next session starts from the state of the work, not from a transcript of it.
Cortex and Neuron. Research and engineering by James Huson. Both at exnulla dot com.
